data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'Justus' meaning 'just' or 'righteous'. In Christianity, it is the name of several saints, including Saint Justina of Padua and Saint Justina of Rome. The name Justiana carries the meaning “Just and righteous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Justiana usually hope their child will grow to embody just and righteous and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Justina the Great, also known as Justina the Elder, was a Roman princess who ruled the Eastern Roman Empire from 523 to 527 AD. She was the first woman to rule the empire and is considered a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church. Justina is known for her patronage of the arts and her promotion of Christianity.
historical_references.context: Justina succeeded her father, Justin I, and ruled during a period of political instability and religious conflict. She faced opposition from the Monophysite and Nestorian factions and worked to promote religious unity within the empire. During her reign, Hagia Sophia was completed, making it one of the most famous and iconic structures of the Byzantine Empire.

historical_references.reference: Saint Justina of Padua, also known as Justina of Silene, was a young Christian martyr who lived in the 3rd century AD. She was the daughter of a pagan Roman nobleman and was raised in a wealthy household in Padua, Italy. She converted to Christianity and was persecuted for her faith, becoming a symbol of Christian resistance and martyrdom. Her relics are venerated in Padua and she is the patron saint of the city.
historical_references.context: Saint Justina's life and martyrdom took place during a time of intense persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire. She was arrested and put on trial for her faith, but refused to recant. She was subjected to various forms of torture and eventually beheaded. Her story became a popular one in Christian literature and she was venerated as a saint and martyr, inspiring many to follow in her footsteps.
